rawFindings.title: Incorrect nulling of exit code bytes in buffer
rawFindings.explanation: The line `tail.fill('\x00')` modifies the tail buffer in-place and nulls the bytes starting at tailPos. However, the subsequent `process.stdout.write(buffer)` writes the entire original buffer including the nulled tail, which could corrupt the displayed output by replacing characters with nulls in stdout.
rawFindings.suggestion: Instead of mutating the original buffer by nulling out the tail, slice the buffer to exclude the exit code portion when writing to stdout, i.e., write `buffer.slice(0, tailPos)` to stdout. Alternatively, copy the buffer before nulling so that the original remains unaffected for output.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Sending test run output that ends with the exit code marker leads to stdout containing null characters at the end of the output, disrupting the readable output.
